title_en: Reading day 1: the formulas of the Rātib and where they come from
q_en: I know these words by ear. Can I read them, understand them and say where they come from?
q_ar: أَعْرِفُ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتِ بِالسَّمْعِ. هَلْ أَقْرَؤُهَا وَأَفْهَمُهَا وَأَعْرِفُ مِنْ أَيْنَ جَاءَتْ؟
not_yet: New grammar: today is a reading day, so nothing new is taught.
Every word of the ḥadīth wordings: the glosses help; the rest comes in later lessons.
The chains of the ḥadīth (who told whom): Lesson 49.
not_yet_ar: قَاعِدَةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ: الْيَوْمُ يَوْمُ قِرَاءَةٍ، وَلَا نَتَعَلَّمُ فِيهِ شَيْئًا جَدِيدًا.
كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي أَلْفَاظِ الْحَدِيثِ: تُعِينُكَ الشُّرُوحُ، وَالْبَاقِي فِي دُرُوسٍ قَادِمَةٍ.

slides.head_en: Look: four words you say every day
slides.head_ar: اُنْظُرْ: أَرْبَعُ كَلِمَاتٍ تَقُولُهَا كُلَّ يَوْمٍ
sents: There is no god but Allah.

lines: Which words in these four lines are nouns? Is there any verb at all?
أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ فِي هَذِهِ الْأَسْطُرِ أَسْمَاءٌ؟ هَلْ فِيهَا فِعْلٌ؟
What is the last word of the first three lines? What does that tell you about these formulas?
مَا آخِرُ كَلِمَةٍ فِي الْأَسْطُرِ الثَّلَاثَةِ الْأُولَى؟ عَلَى مَاذَا يَدُلُّ ذَلِكَ فِي هَذِهِ الْأَذْكَارِ؟
You have said these words for years. Which line did you not know the meaning of until today?
قُلْتَ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتِ سِنِينَ. أَيُّ سَطْرٍ لَمْ تَعْرِفْ مَعْنَاهُ إِلَى الْيَوْمِ؟

slides.head_en: Four small keys: no new grammar today
slides.head_ar: أَرْبَعَةُ مَفَاتِيحَ صَغِيرَةٍ: لَا قَاعِدَةَ جَدِيدَةَ الْيَوْمَ

cards.def_en: One name follows, ending in ـِ.

slides.head_en: The same words in the ḥadīth and in the Rātib
slides.head_ar: الْأَلْفَاظُ نَفْسُهَا فِي الْحَدِيثِ وَفِي الرَّاتِبِ
rows: His is the dominion and His the praise
لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ
the same, and the Rātib adds: He gives life and causes death
slides.tip: The Rātib may change “whoever” to “we”, or add words found in another narration (al-Tirmidhī 3474).
slides.tip_ar: الرَّاتِبُ يُحَوِّلُ «مَنْ» إِلَى «نَحْنُ»، وَقَدْ يَزِيدُ أَلْفَاظًا وَرَدَتْ فِي رِوَايَةٍ أُخْرَى.

lines: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ،
1 · There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner;
لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ،
His is the dominion and His the praise; He gives life and causes death,
and He has power over all things.
2 · Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah,
وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَاللهُ أَكْبَرُ
and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest.
3 · Glory be to Allah and with His praise;
glory be to Allah, the Tremendous.
4 · I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah
from the evil of what He created.
5 · In the name of Allah, with whose
وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
or in heaven can cause harm; and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
6 · We are pleased with Allah as Lord,
with Islam as religion and with Muḥammad as Prophet.

rows: Muslim 2708: on stopping at a place
Abū Dāwūd 5088: the name that brings no harm
Muslim 1884: pleased with Allah as Lord
slides.note: The ḥadīth wording is the source; the Rātib gathers these words into one daily wird.
slides.note_ar: أَلْفَاظُ الْحَدِيثِ هِيَ الْأَصْلُ، وَالرَّاتِبُ يَجْمَعُهَا فِي وِرْدٍ يَوْمِيٍّ.

slides.head_en: Two clauses of ḥadīth behind the formulas
lines: أَحَبُّ الْكَلَامِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَرْبَعٌ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
“The dearest words to Allah are four: glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest.”
مَنْ رَضِيَ بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيًّا
“Whoever is pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion and with Muḥammad as Prophet, the Garden becomes his due.”

slides.head_en: Try: what does each word mean?

slides.why: A student reads this without looking at the last word. After the word “in” the ending is a kasra (ـِ), so the last word must end in ـِ. Look at the endings before you read a line aloud.
slides.why_ar: قَرَأَ طَالِبٌ هَذِهِ الْجُمْلَةَ وَلَمْ يَنْتَبِهْ لِآخِرِ الْكَلِمَةِ. بَعْدَ «فِي» الْكَسْرَةُ: فِي الرِّبَاطِ. اُنْظُرْ إِلَى النِّهَايَاتِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقْرَأَ.

can: I can read the six formulas of the Rātib and say what each one means.
I can say, for each formula, which ḥadīth it comes from.
can_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ أَذْكَارَ الرَّاتِبِ السِّتَّةَ وَأَقُولَ مَعْنَى كُلِّ ذِكْرٍ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقُولَ مِنْ أَيِّ حَدِيثٍ جَاءَ كُلُّ ذِكْرٍ.

sections.name: A
sections.en: Read the six formulas of the Rātib aloud, then answer.
lines: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His the praise; He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things.
سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَاللهُ أَكْبَرُ
Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest.
سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، سُبْحَانَ اللهِ الْعَظِيمِ
Glory be to Allah and with His praise; glory be to Allah, the Tremendous.
أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created.
بِسْمِ اللهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
رَضِينَا بِاللهِ رَبًّا، وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا، وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيًّا
We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion and with Muḥammad as Prophet.
sections.source: Rātib al-Ḥaddād, six of its dhikrs (each said three times)

Sources of the lines: (1) Muslim 2691, al-Tirmidhī 3474; (2) Muslim 2137; (3) Muslim 2694, al-Bukhārī 6406; (4) Muslim 2708; (5) Abū Dāwūd 5088; (6) Muslim 1884.

items.en: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
items.model: Short dhikr formulas from the Rātib of Imam ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥaddād; each one is also found in a ḥadīth.

items.en: Line 1: whose is the dominion, and whose is the praise?
options: Allah’s: “His is the dominion and His the praise”.
The first: Glory be to Allah. The last: Allah is greatest.
items.answer: Allah’s: “His is the dominion and His the praise”.
items.model: Allah’s: “His is the dominion and His the praise”.

options: The first: Glory be to Allah. The last: Allah is greatest.
السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ: the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

items.en: Line 2 joins four short formulas with وَ. Say the first and the last.
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٢: يَجْمَعُ أَرْبَعَةَ أَذْكَارٍ. اُذْكُرِ الْأَوَّلَ وَالْأَخِيرَ.
options: Allah’s: “His is the dominion and His the praise”.
The first: Glory be to Allah. The last: Allah is greatest.
items.answer: The first: Glory be to Allah. The last: Allah is greatest.
items.model: The first: Glory be to Allah. The last: Allah is greatest.
Glory be to Allah and with His praise; glory be to Allah, the Tremendous.

items.en: True or false? Line 3 says that Allah is small.
items.ar_q: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ السَّطْرُ ٣ يَقُولُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ صَغِيرٌ.

items.en: Line 4: from the evil of what? In whose perfect words do we seek refuge?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٤: مِنْ شَرِّ مَاذَا؟ وَبِكَلِمَاتِ مَنْ نَعُوذُ؟
items.model: From the evil of what He created; in the perfect words of Allah.

items.en: Which line speaks about the earth and the sky?
options: The first: Glory be to Allah. The last: Allah is greatest.
Allah’s: “His is the dominion and His the praise”.

items.en: Line 5: two names of Allah end the line. Which two?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٥: يَنْتَهِي بِاسْمَيْنِ لِلَّهِ. مَا هُمَا؟
options: السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ: the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
Allah’s: “His is the dominion and His the praise”.
items.answer: السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ: the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
items.model: السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ: the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

items.en: Line 6: with what are we pleased? Name the three.
items.model: With Allah as Lord, Islam as religion and Muḥammad as Prophet.

items.en: True or false? Every one of the six lines names Allah.
items.ar_q: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ فِي كُلِّ سَطْرٍ مِنَ الْأَسْطُرِ السِّتَّةِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ.
items.model: True: every line contains the name Allāh.
items.note: every line contains the name Allāh.

items.en: ★ Line 6: these three words end in the same way. What is the ending, and what does it tell you?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٦: لِهَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتِ الثَّلَاثِ النِّهَايَةُ نَفْسُهَا. مَا هِيَ؟ وَمَاذَا تَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ؟
items.model: Tanwīn with fatḥa (ـًا). The three words play the same part: each says what we are pleased with.

items.en: ★ Line 1 has two verbs side by side with opposite meanings. What are they, and what do they say about Allah?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ١: فِعْلَانِ مُتَقَابِلَانِ. مَا هُمَا؟ وَمَاذَا يَقُولَانِ عَنِ اللَّهِ؟
items.model: He gives life and He causes death: all life and death are in His hand.

sections.name: B
sections.en: Behind the formulas: two clauses of ḥadīth from Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim. Read, then answer.
lines: أَحَبُّ الْكَلَامِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَرْبَعٌ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
“The dearest words to Allah are four: glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest.”
مَنْ رَضِيَ بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيًّا
“Whoever is pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion and with Muḥammad as Prophet, the Garden becomes his due.”

items.en: How many words does clause 1 call “the dearest to Allah”?

items.model: Glory be to Allah; praise belongs to Allah; there is no god but Allah; Allah is greatest.

items.en: Which line of the Rātib (lines 1–6) gives these four words together?

options: Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, Muḥammad as Prophet.

items.en: Clause 2 begins with مَنْ. What does مَنْ mean here?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ الثَّانِي يَبْدَأُ بِـ «مَنْ». مَا مَعْنَاهَا هُنَا؟
options: Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, Muḥammad as Prophet.

items.en: With what is the person pleased in clause 2? Name the three.
items.ar_q: بِمَاذَا يَرْضَى الْإِنْسَانُ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟
options: Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, Muḥammad as Prophet.
items.answer: Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, Muḥammad as Prophet.
items.model: Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, Muḥammad as Prophet.

items.en: True or false? The Rātib says رَضِيَ (“whoever is pleased”) in line 6, exactly as in the ḥadīth.
items.ar_q: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ يَقُولُ الرَّاتِبُ «رَضِيَ» كَمَا فِي الْحَدِيثِ.
items.model: False. The Rātib says رَضِينَا, “we are pleased”.
items.note: The Rātib says رَضِينَا, “we are pleased”.

items.en: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ النَّصِّ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
items.model: A ḥadīth (the words of the Prophet ﷺ), from Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, nos. 2137 and 1884.

items.en: ★ The words أَكْبَرُ and أَحَبُّ both begin with أَ and mean “most …”. What do they have in common?
items.ar_q: فِي كَلِمَتَيْ «أَكْبَرُ» وَ«أَحَبُّ» وَزْنٌ وَاحِدٌ. مَا هُوَ؟
items.model: Both are on the same pattern, the one that means “more …” or “most …” (greatest, dearest).

items.en: ★ Clause 1 of the ḥadīth and line 2 of the Rātib give the same four words. Is the order the same?
options: Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, Muḥammad as Prophet.

sections.name: C
sections.en: A night in the ribāṭ. You have not seen this text. Read it aloud, then answer. (Word: أَسْتَغْفِرُ = I ask forgiveness.)
lines: فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
At night Ahmad sat with the students in the ribāṭ.
The Habib opened the book and read the Rātib.
وَقَالَ الطُّلَّابُ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ.
And the students said: There is no god but Allah.
ثُمَّ سَبَّحَ أَحْمَدُ وَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ وَكَبَّرَ.
Then Ahmad glorified Allah, praised Him and said Allāhu akbar.
And he said: I ask Allah for forgiveness.
سَمِعَ الضُّيُوفُ الذِّكْرَ، وَكَانَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ سَعِيدَةً.
The guests heard the dhikr, and their hearts were happy.
The Habib said: Dhikr is a light for the heart.
And Ahmad returned to the house and slept.

items.en: Who sat with the students, and where?

items.en: What did the students say in line 3?
options: He glorified Allah, praised Him and said Allāhu akbar.
There is no god but Allah.

items.model: There is no god but Allah.

items.en: Put in order: (a) Ahmad glorified Allah (b) the Habib read the Rātib (c) Ahmad returned to the house.
items.ar_q: رَتِّبِ الْأَحْدَاثَ: (أ) سَبَّحَ أَحْمَدُ (ب) قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ الرَّاتِبَ (ج) رَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ.
options: He glorified Allah, praised Him and said Allāhu akbar.
There is no god but Allah.

items.en: Line 4 has three verbs. What did Ahmad do?
items.ar_q: فِي السَّطْرِ ٤ ثَلَاثَةُ أَفْعَالٍ. مَاذَا فَعَلَ أَحْمَدُ؟
options: There is no god but Allah.
He glorified Allah, praised Him and said Allāhu akbar.
items.answer: He glorified Allah, praised Him and said Allāhu akbar.
items.model: He glorified Allah, praised Him and said Allāhu akbar.

sections.name: Y
sections.en: The Story Strip: lines 1–76
lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.
The Habib sat in the mosque.
The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
The boy came in through the door.
The mother looked at the boy.
The boy sits in the study circle today.
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
The boy was happy in the majlis.
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
